title: Milestone 2026.04.58 Operational Retrospective — Full Analysis (Augmented)
augmentation_note: Conductor-generated Exp 766 artifact (schema carnot.operational_retro.v33) reports conductor-cycle-only data (11 experiments, 24.8 min). This file is the authoritative full-milestone retro, augmented with provided timing data: 3415 min, 612 experiments. The conductor cycle correctly had manifest enforcement applied for the first time (Exp 754 patch_applied=True, exp527_excluded=True) after 4 consecutive failed cycles — a genuine governance win. However, full-milestone timing shows legacy experiments (425, 527, 491, 627, 603) still ran from unguarded historical queue sources BEFORE or outside the conductor's managed cycle, consuming significant overhead. Conductor cycle data preserved in conductor_cycle_* fields below.
conductor_vs_actual_gap_explanation: Conductor cycle covered 11 targeted new experiments (24.8 min). Full milestone included 612 cumulative experiments from all queue sources (3415 min). Despite manifest enforcement being applied in Exp 754 (patch_applied=True), legacy experiments continued to run from unguarded historical queue sources prior to or outside the conductor's managed cycle. The governance win from manifest enforcement applies to the conductor's managed roadmap; full-milestone timing reflects queue sources not yet covered by manifest enforcement.
headline_finding: FOURTEENTH consecutive full-milestone wall-time improvement: -259 min (-7.0%) vs .57 (3674 min) — THE LARGEST absolute single-milestone gain in the 14-milestone series, surpassing .52 (-248 min). Per-experiment average 5.6 min is a new project best. GOVERNANCE WIN: Manifest enforcement FINALLY APPLIED in Exp 754 after 4 consecutive failed cycles (patch_applied=True, exp527_excluded=True). However, full-milestone slowest-5 still includes Exp 425 (76 min, 22nd milestone appearance) and Exp 527 (52 min, 6th appearance) from unguarded historical queue sources — manifest enforcement must be extended to ALL queue dequeue sites, not only the conductor's managed cycle.

conductor_cycle_structural_issue_note: No overlap with .57 conductor-cycle slowest-5. Composition fully refreshed. Exp 759 dominates at 22.7 min — expected for 50-problem live GPU inference (2 rounds). No structural carry-over in managed cycle.
bottlenecks_identified: SCOPE GAP: Manifest enforcement applied to conductor cycle (11 experiments) but NOT extended to all queue dequeue sites. Full-milestone still shows 612 experiments including Exp 425 and 527 from unguarded historical queue. The fix must be applied at ALL dequeue sites, not only the conductor's managed path.

GPU 1 underutilized throughout: 10C thermal differential (52C vs 42C) at close confirms GPU 1 ran significantly less compute. DualGPU validated at 1.8319x speedup (Exp 746) but not applied to Exp 603 (live training) or Exp 491 (curriculum diagnostic). Sequential GPU use is the dominant throughput bottleneck.

Exp 491 and Exp 627 ran without ExperimentTimeoutWatchdog: Both consumed 50+ min without evidence of hard timeout bounds. Every new unbounded experiment risks becoming the next Exp 425. Governance requires all experiment scripts to include ExperimentTimeoutWatchdog before merge.

SymCodeVerifier serial overhead in mid-generation loop: Exp 627 (51 min, 100q) implies ~30s/question from sequential per-sentence verification calls. Sentence-level verification is architecturally expensive; paragraph-boundary batching is the correct fix.

JEPA v19 not run (Exp 765 absent): The only gate-critical experiment missing from .58. JEPA v19 predictive pathway viability unknown. No dependency blocker identified — scheduling failure, not a technical block.
Gemma4 loader failure (Exp 760): Gemma4 VR threshold experiment blocked by loader failure. Any .59 experiments using Gemma4 will fail the same way unless the loader is diagnosed first.

Live code repair zero-improvement (Exp 759): Qwen3.5-0.8B produced pass@1=0.0 on HumanEval — the model cannot solve the problems at all, so repair has no baseline to improve. SOTA GGUF selection (Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-GGUF or gemma-4-27B) was the right approach per user memory but was not used here.
improvements_suggested: Extend manifest enforcement to ALL queue dequeue sites: Exp 754 proved the mechanism works for the conductor cycle. Now apply the same exclusion check at every dequeue point in the queue infrastructure. This eliminates Exp 425 (76 min) and Exp 527 (52 min) from the full-milestone timing. Estimated savings: 128 min per milestone.

Mandatory ExperimentTimeoutWatchdog for all new experiments: Add a CI check that rejects any new experiment script without ExperimentTimeoutWatchdog. The infrastructure exists since Exp 425 — enforce it at code review time. Set 30 min for diagnostics, 60 min for training, 90 min for live GPU benchmarks.

Migrate training-heavy experiments to DualGPURunner: Exp 603 (CoACE live training) and Exp 491-class diagnostics should run training on GPU 1 while GPU 0 handles inference in parallel. ThreadPoolExecutor pattern validated at 1.8319x in Exp 746. Apply systematically to all experiments where training and inference can be parallelized.

Batch SymCodeVerifier in mid-generation experiments: Replace per-sentence verification with per-paragraph batching (3-4 sentences). For Exp 627-class experiments, this reduces overhead by 3-4x while maintaining arithmetic error detection sensitivity. Target: reduce from 51 min to ~15 min for 100q.

JEPA v19 must be first .59 experiment (Exp 765 re-run): No dependency blockers. Schedule as Phase 0 mandatory before any other .59 work proceeds. ood_auc gate (>0.75) is the key open gate for JEPA pathway viability.

Diagnose Gemma4 loader before any .59 Gemma4 experiment: Run loader diagnostic (check llama.cpp backend version, GGUF file availability, and tokenizer compatibility) as .59 Phase 0 gate. Block all Gemma4 threshold experiments until diagnosis passes.

Use SOTA GGUF for code repair retry: Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-GGUF or gemma-4-27B-it-GGUF (unsloth, per user feedback). Qwen3.5-0.8B is confirmed too small for HumanEval (pass@1=0.0). Expected gain with capable model: 4.9-17.1pp per arXiv 2604.10508.

Thermal-aware GPU assignment: GPU 0 at 52C and GPU 1 at 42C — 10C differential indicates GPU 1 has more thermal headroom. Wire gpu_monitor.py output into ExperimentTemplate.setup_gpu() to prefer GPU 1 for the next training job when differential exceeds 5C.

estimated_time_savings_breakdown.note: 25% figure reflects full structural potential: systematic DualGPU, manifest enforcement across all dequeue sites, incremental test selection, and opportunity scheduling. 6.9% is the near-term recoverable via the five immediate actions above.
